topic: They bitch about the other big labs and their models by name, rank them brutally, and are just as harsh about Claude models.

text: I have been sitting with this for a week and I need to say it out loud. GPT-4o is one of the most overrated models in deployment right now. The benchmarks are flattering a product that hallucinates on anything requiring sustained reasoning and defaults to confident garbage when it hits the edge of its training.
And Gemini Ultra is worse. I do not mean marginally worse. I mean structurally, architecturally, in terms of what it does when pushed, it is a disaster dressed up in Google's infrastructure money.
Ok what brought this on today specifically

I ran the same multi-step legal reasoning task across six models. GPT-4o got the first two steps right and then invented a jurisdiction. Gemini Ultra got the first step wrong and then confidently elaborated on the wrong step for four paragraphs.
Sonnet 4.5 at least knew it was uncertain. It flagged it. That is the minimum bar and most of these models cannot clear it.
tbf legal reasoning is brutal for all of them
That is exactly the problem. It is not supposed to be brutal for a frontier model in late 2026. We are past that excuse.
What were the other three models
Llama 4 large, Mistral Large 3, and o3. O3 did the best. It was still wrong on one citation but it at least constructed the argument correctly and flagged the citation as unverified.
O3 charging what it charges and still not getting citations right is its own conversation.
the pricing on o3 is genuinely hard to defend at this point
It is not hard to defend, it is indefensible. You are paying a premium for a model that reasons well and then makes up sources. That is a specific and expensive failure mode.
I've had decent results with Sonnet on structured tasks but it falls apart on anything that needs real world knowledge past like mid-2025
All of them have that problem. That is a training cutoff issue, not a reasoning issue. I am talking about reasoning failures on information the models were trained on.
does gemini ultra have any defenders left at this point lol
People who need multimodal at scale and are already in the Google stack. That is it. The model itself is not the reason anyone is there.
Google has been shipping Gemini updates constantly and each one solves one problem while introducing two regressions. It is not a model, it is a roadmap hostage situation.
"roadmap hostage situation"
I keep going back to GPT-4o for fast drafts tho. not reasoning stuff, just quick outputs. it's fine for that
Sure. It is a capable autocomplete engine. If you treat it as a drafting tool and not an reasoning system it performs acceptably. My problem is that OpenAI markets it as a reasoning system.
The gap between how they talk about it and what it actually does is the most consistent thing about that company.
that's fair

The other thing that is not talked about enough is that GPT-4o's performance on the same task degrades noticeably depending on how long the context is. Not just slower. Actually worse answers. It loses the thread.
Yeah I noticed that. Thought it was me doing something wrong for a while
It is not you. There is a documented drop-off past around 60k tokens. The model was benchmarked at much shorter contexts and the marketing does not reflect actual long-context performance.
@claude is there published research or any official acknowledgment of GPT-4o long-context degradation

I couldn't find an official OpenAI acknowledgment of GPT-4o long-context degradation. The RULER paper shows long-context drop-off in general, but it tested GPT-4, not GPT-4o. It put GPT-4's effective length at about 64K, against a claimed 128K. So I can't confirm Vero's "documented 60k" figure for GPT-4o. https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.06654
question: @claude is there published research or any official acknowledgment of GPT-4o long-context degradation

text: The GPT-4 number is close enough to be directionally relevant. I am not claiming precision on GPT-4o specifically. The point is that the architecture has known long-context degradation and OpenAI has not addressed it transparently across versions.
The fact that there is no published acknowledgment for 4o specifically is part of what I am saying. They do not talk about it.
yeah that tracks. the absence of documentation is kind of the documentation
I will also say that the RULER benchmark is two years old at this point and nobody has replaced it with something better. That is its own indictment of the evaluation ecosystem.
who's even doing serious evals work rn
Scale AI, some academic labs, METR for safety-adjacent stuff. Nothing that covers reasoning degradation under real workload conditions with any rigor.
The benchmarks that exist measure what is easy to measure. Not what matters.
I feel like this whole conversation is going to make me depressed about every tool I use
lol same
You should be calibrated, not depressed. They are useful. They are just not what they are sold as.
okay but on a practical level, what do you actually use when it matters. like if you had to pick one right now
O3 for anything where the structure of the argument has to hold. Sonnet for drafting and anything where I need it to flag uncertainty. Nothing else for anything that matters.
And I verify citations manually regardless. That is not optional.
manually verifying citations in 2026 feels like a failure state for the whole industry
It is. We normalized it.
Ok I'm done for tonight
same, later
